title: Combine lighting gels to match a reference colour
instruction: Stack gels in the outlined area until its light matches the colour of the reference light. Do not move the reference.
context: Theatre and studio lighting technicians pick colour-correction gels off a rack and combine them to hit a colour a designer has specified, judging the result on a lightbox before it goes in the lantern. Two gels together transmit the product of their colours, so the choice cannot be made by matching any single gel to the target: the technician has to predict what a combination will look like. Getting it wrong means a re-rig between performances.
setup: Fixed station, metres: x forward, y left, z up; heights are relative to the tabletop. Four loose gel frames, 50 g each, 60 x 60 x 20 mm, start at amber (0.150, 0.280), cyan (0.330, 0.280), violet (0.150, -0.330) and lime (0.330, -0.330). Each is a 4 mm clear acrylic glazing on four PLA rails 8 mm wide and 16 mm high, leaving a 44 x 44 mm aperture; the rails are tinted with that gel's colour, which is how each gel is identified. Two fixed white acrylic lightboxes, 120 x 120 x 10 mm, are centred at (0.300, 0.055) and (0.300, -0.145), each with a 44 x 44 mm lit window in its top face. A 60 x 60 mm dark square outline, 2 mm wide and 0.2 mm high, marks the first box. The second carries a fixed reference assembly: two clear 50 g frames of the same construction, stacked, so the reference is seen through the same two glazings as a correct two-gel stack. Gels start 1 mm above their supports to settle.
scoring: A gel counts as stacked when it is glazing-up within 10 degrees of horizontal, centred within 1 cm per axis of the outlined square, still for 20 control steps, and its lowest corner is within 3 mm of the top of its support (the lightbox, or the gel below). 1.0 when the stacked gels together transmit the reference colour and nothing else is touching them; 0.5 when they do but an extra gel is also on or against the stack; 0.25 when the stack is part of a correct combination with no extra touching it; 0.0 otherwise, including an empty outline. Credit follows the transmitted colour, not specific gels, so any combination that reproduces the reference scores full marks; with this gel set that is amber plus cyan, in either order. Moving the reference more than 5 mm or 5 degrees from its pose at reset scores 0 for the trial, even if it is put back.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. The reset restores all gels to their starting layout, clears the reference-moved latch and the stillness history, and re-records the reference pose.
fidelity: Rigid framed gels, lit lightbox windows and a pose-based scorer. The renderer does not composite stacked transmissive sheets, so the glazing is clear and each window is lit with the gel colours above it multiplied componentwise, rather than ray traced. Scoring uses pose, not contact: a gel held steady within the 3 mm support tolerance can count as placed.
